subtype: Approach: keeps the value and rebuilds the route in stages [Revision]
passage:
Payal sat with Akash, her old manager, in the office canteen. "I quit too fast last time," she said. "I still want to work with village clinics. That hasn't changed."

Akash asked how she would go about it this time.

"In stages. First, part-time here, three days a week. Second, saving for a year so my parents' expenses stay covered. Third, weekends with the rural health group, doing whatever help they need: registers, bookings, driving."

"And then?"

"After a year I decide whether to move over fully, based on what I actually see."

Akash nodded. "Sounds slow."

"It is," said Payal. "But I'm still going in the same direction."

qa.q: How many days a week will Payal work part-time?
qa.a: Payal will work part-time three days a week.

qa.q: How does Payal seem to feel about her earlier decision?
qa.a: Payal seems regretful but still determined, since she says she quit too fast but still wants the work.

qa.q: What could Payal check during the year of volunteering?
qa.a: Payal could check whether the work suits her day to day, and whether money and family needs can be covered if she moves over fully.

qa.q: How might Akash see Payal's new plan?
qa.a: Akash may feel reassured, seeing Payal keep her aim while taking slow steps.

grounding: Shows a person keeping her value and rebuilding the route in stages, working part-time and volunteering before a bigger shift.
